safe.label: All lakes · on trails
safe.intro: Minaret, Ediza, Garnet and Thousand Island, connected on mapped trails. The extra approach and JMT bypass make this a demanding four-day trip.
safe.recommendation: Best match for seeing every lake while avoiding the Cecile scramble. Only commit after access and conditions checks; the roughly 23-mile exit exceeds your 20-mile daily aim.

days.title: Horseshoe → Minaret
days.summary: Mammoth Pass, Upper Crater Meadow, JMT and Minaret Creek.
directions: Start at Horseshoe Lake / Mammoth Pass trailhead, after parking and road access are confirmed.
Cross Mammoth Pass; use the cutoff toward Upper Crater Meadow and the JMT/PCT. The map uses this longer approach, not the direct resort spur.
Follow the ranger-confirmed open northbound trail connection through the Postpile area to Minaret Creek.
Take Minaret Creek upstream to Minaret Lake. Select a legal durable site, away from water and trail.
days.warning: The trail line is mapped; it does not establish permission to pass through the construction area.

days.title: Minaret → Ediza via JMT
days.summary: Retrace Minaret Creek, then JMT north and the Ediza branch.
directions: Retrace Minaret Creek to its JMT junction.
Follow the JMT north through the Rosalie / Gladys lake country to the Shadow Creek–Ediza junction.
Follow the Ediza branch west to the lake. Use legal west-side camping, outside the posted restricted areas.
No Cecile traverse, cross-country ridge shortcut or peak summit is included. Any separate Iceberg outing must remain on the established trail from Ediza and requires its own conditions check.
days.warning: About 14 mapped miles, rather than the short Cecile connection. Start early and retain daylight margin.

days.title: Ediza → Garnet → Thousand Island
days.summary: JMT north, Ruby / Emerald, then return to Garnet.
directions: Return from Ediza to the JMT and turn north toward Garnet. Do not cut directly over the ridge between the lake pins.
Continue on mapped trails to the Garnet lake area. Legal camps require a shoreline detour outside the outlet exclusion.
Visit Thousand Island via the JMT, Ruby and Emerald lakes; enjoy the Banner Peak views.
Return on the same trail to Garnet. Skip the Thousand Island out-and-back if you are behind schedule.
days.warning: GIS estimates include representative shoreline trail points. Guide distances to lake outlets are shorter; campsite choice changes this day.

days.title: Garnet → Horseshoe
days.summary: Long southbound return on JMT and Mammoth Pass.
directions: Follow the JMT south past the Ediza junction and the Minaret Creek junction.
Use the same ranger-confirmed legal approach through the Postpile area.
Continue to Upper Crater Meadow and reverse the cutoff over Mammoth Pass.
Finish at Horseshoe Lake. Do not depend on Friday transport from a Reds Meadow road-access trailhead.
days.warning: Roughly 23 mapped miles before campsite detours. This is the limiting day for a three-night plan.

short.label: Minaret focus
short.intro: Use Minaret as your scenic focus, then return the same way. This preserves the Minarets while reducing the number of high lake basins and the long Friday exit.
short.recommendation: My more conservative choice with this forecast, if the access and footing checks pass. It is still an alpine trip, not a weather-safe refuge. Descend or exit early if conditions worsen.

days.title: Minaret basin · flexible day
days.summary: Rest, shoreline viewpoints or an early descent.
directions: Assess the actual snow, wind and accessible water before adding an outing.
Stay on the established Minaret Lake trail and accessible trail-side viewpoints. No Cecile traverse, off-trail shoreline scrambling, ridge shortcut or peak summit is included.
If the weather or footing deteriorates, start the same-trail exit. Three nights are a preference, not a reason to remain exposed.
days.warning: No extra exploration miles are counted. Legal intermediate camping may split the approach or return, but locations require ranger confirmation.

days.title: Minaret basin · flexible day
days.summary: A second scenic day, or shorten the wilderness trip.
directions: Reassess the forecast and footing. Remain in legal sites and keep the same-trail retreat available.
Photograph the basin from accessible durable terrain. Do not treat historical photos as proof of current conditions.
Be willing to leave earlier than Friday rather than force the original schedule.
days.warning: The map intentionally adds no fabricated exploration loop or guaranteed bad-weather campsite.

days.title: Minaret → Horseshoe
days.summary: Reverse the confirmed entry approach.
directions: Descend Minaret Creek to the JMT.
Reverse the ranger-confirmed legal trail connection through the Postpile area and Upper Crater Meadow.
Cross Mammoth Pass and return to the Horseshoe trailhead.
days.warning: The exit is still about 16 mapped miles, with climbing back over Mammoth Pass. Start early.

rush.label: Rush Creek · northern lakes
rush.intro: Enter near Silver Lake and focus on Thousand Island and Garnet. This changes the trailhead and avoids dependence on the Reds Meadow approach.
rush.recommendation: An access alternative, not a snow workaround. It requires a Rush Creek AA05 permit, a separately confirmed parking plan, and current high-country conditions.
camp: Thousand Island Lake area, or retreat

days.title: Rush Creek → Thousand Island
days.summary: Silver Lake trailhead, reservoir country and the PCT/JMT.
directions: Confirm overnight parking at Rush Creek trailhead near Silver Lake on Highway 158 and reserve the correct entry permit.
Follow Rush Creek past Agnew and Gem lakes toward Waugh, then join the PCT/JMT and continue over Island Pass to Thousand Island. This map excludes the Clark / Spooky Meadow shortcuts.
Reach Thousand Island Lake and select a legal site outside the quarter-mile outlet exclusion.
days.warning: This itinerary is a separate permit and high-country route. The final mapped approach is described in the geometry source notes.

days.title: Thousand Island ↔ Garnet
days.summary: Optional JMT outing past Emerald and Ruby.
directions: Follow the JMT south via Emerald and Ruby to Garnet.
Return on the same trail to your legal Thousand Island campsite.
Omit this outing if snow, ice, wind or daylight reduces your margin.
days.warning: Omitting Garnet reduces the total; actual camp and shoreline detours are extra.

days.title: Northern lakes · flexible day
days.summary: Lake viewpoints, rest, or an earlier exit.
directions: Keep exploration on accessible mapped trails and durable terrain.
Reassess cold, wind, water access and your exit margin.
If conditions deteriorate, exit on the confirmed entry trail.
days.warning: No summit or off-trail pass is needed to enjoy the lake basin.

days.title: Thousand Island → Rush Creek
days.summary: Reverse the mapped entry trail to Silver Lake.
directions: Return by the same confirmed route through the Rush Creek drainage.
Finish at your authorized Silver Lake parking location.
days.warning: Confirm Highway 158 access and parking before departure; the permit does not guarantee either.

balanced.label: All lakes · more even days
balanced.intro: Keep every major lake, return to Ediza Thursday, and leave from there Friday. This trades more total walking for a less concentrated exit.
balanced.recommendation: If all-lake scenery is the priority and the access / conditions checks pass, this spreads the walking more evenly: about 16 / 14 / 19 / 20 mapped miles. The ~20-mile exit is before campsite detours, so it is not a strict 20-mile cap.

days.title: Horseshoe → Minaret
days.summary: Mammoth Pass, Upper Crater Meadow, JMT and Minaret Creek.
directions: Start at Horseshoe Lake / Mammoth Pass trailhead, after parking and road access are confirmed.
Cross Mammoth Pass; use the cutoff toward Upper Crater Meadow and the JMT/PCT. The map uses this longer approach, not the direct resort spur.
Follow the ranger-confirmed open northbound trail connection through the Postpile area to Minaret Creek.
Take Minaret Creek upstream to Minaret Lake. Select a legal durable site, away from water and trail.
days.warning: The trail line is mapped; it does not establish permission to pass through the construction area.

days.title: Minaret → Ediza via JMT
days.summary: Retrace Minaret Creek, then JMT north and the Ediza branch.
directions: Retrace Minaret Creek to its JMT junction.
Follow the JMT north through the Rosalie / Gladys lake country to the Shadow Creek–Ediza junction.
Follow the Ediza branch west to the lake. Use legal west-side camping, outside the posted restricted areas.
No Cecile traverse, cross-country ridge shortcut or peak summit is included. Any separate Iceberg outing must remain on the established trail from Ediza and requires its own conditions check.
days.warning: About 14 mapped miles, rather than the short Cecile connection. Start early and retain daylight margin.

days.title: Ediza ↔ Thousand Island via Garnet
days.summary: JMT lake tour, then return to Ediza for a shorter Friday.
directions: Leave your legal Ediza camp and follow the Ediza branch back to the JMT. Turn north toward Garnet.
Visit Garnet, Ruby / Emerald and Thousand Island on the mapped trail itinerary.
Return on the same trails past Garnet to Ediza for your third night.
Skip Thousand Island or turn around sooner if you are behind schedule; this is a long out-and-back.
days.warning: Roughly 19 mapped miles with several climbs. It adds total walking but avoids moving your third-night camp farther north.

days.title: Ediza → Horseshoe
days.summary: JMT south, Upper Crater approach and Mammoth Pass.
directions: Return from Ediza to the JMT and follow it south through the lake country.
Use the same ranger-confirmed legal connection through the Postpile area to Upper Crater Meadow.
Reverse the cutoff and Mammoth Pass approach to Horseshoe Lake.
days.warning: Approximately 20 mapped miles, before campsite and shoreline detours. More even than the Garnet exit, but still a substantial final day.

duck.label: Duck Pass · Purple & Silver Divide
duck.intro: A no-shuttle lake tour south of Mammoth: Duck Pass, Purple Lake, Lake Virginia and the Silver Divide near Chief Lake. Return by the same trails.
duck.recommendation: A strong shorter scenic alternative if Lake Mary Road, Coldwater parking and current pass footing are confirmed. All miles are mapped trail estimates; actual legal camps and shore detours add distance.

days.title: Coldwater → Purple
days.summary: Duck Pass and the southbound JMT/PCT.
directions: Start from the Duck Pass trailhead at Coldwater after checking the exact legal overnight parking space and seasonal road access.
Follow Duck Pass past the lake basin; descend the Duck Pass trail to the JMT/PCT junction and turn south toward Purple Lake.
Camp on durable ground outside the 300-foot Purple outlet exclusion and at least 100 feet from water and trail.
days.warning: Snow and ice can make an established trail impassable. This is a planning itinerary, not current field clearance.

days.title: Purple → Chief
days.summary: Lake Virginia, Tully Hole and the Silver Divide.
directions: Follow the southbound JMT/PCT past Lake Virginia and down to Tully Hole.
Continue toward the Silver Divide and the mapped trail point near Chief Lake. Do not invent a direct lake-to-lake shortcut.
Choose a legal established site near Chief; the pin is a basin reference, not a marked campsite.
days.warning: Snow and ice can make an established trail impassable. This is a planning itinerary, not current field clearance. The mapped endpoint is near the lake, not its shoreline; campsite approach is extra.

days.title: Chief → Duck
days.summary: Reverse the lake corridor to Duck.
directions: Reverse the JMT/PCT through Tully Hole, Lake Virginia and Purple.
Turn onto the Duck Pass branch and climb into the Duck Lake basin.
Use a legal site away from the 300-foot Duck outlet exclusion. Avoid turning a long day into an unplanned summit outing.
days.warning: Snow and ice can make an established trail impassable. This is a planning itinerary, not current field clearance.

days.title: Duck → Coldwater
days.summary: Cross Duck Pass and descend to the car.
directions: Retrace the Duck Pass trail to Coldwater.
Use the same authorized parking arrangement; no shuttle is required.
days.warning: Snow and ice can make an established trail impassable. This is a planning itinerary, not current field clearance.

checks.title: Confirm Coldwater overnight parking and Lake Mary Road
checks.body: Ask for the exact overnight spaces and Oct 13–16 seasonal access. Do not assume campground parking is available.

checks.title: Reserve JM01 for Oct 13, one person
checks.body: Book the matching entry, exit Oct 16 and one continuous trip. Browser quota snapshot is not a reservation.

checks.title: Get a fresh snow, ice and water report
checks.body: Duck Pass and the Silver Divide are exposed. Confirm footing and legal outlet setbacks at Duck and Purple.

mcgee.label: McGee Pass · Tully & Virginia
mcgee.intro: Autumn canyon, Big McGee Lake, a high pass and Tully basin; visit Lake Virginia before returning to the same trailhead.
mcgee.recommendation: An appealing no-shuttle alternative, with a significant high-pass commitment. Crossing McGee Pass twice is conditional on dry, stable footing and a current report; it is not a snow workaround.

days.title: McGee Creek → Big McGee
days.summary: Canyon ascent and the lake branch.
directions: Reach McGee Creek trailhead at the end of McGee Creek Road after checking road condition and overnight parking permission.
Follow McGee Pass trail up the canyon and take the mapped Big McGee Lake branch.
Select durable legal ground at least 100 feet from water and trail.
days.warning: Snow and ice can make an established trail impassable. This is a planning itinerary, not current field clearance.

days.title: Big McGee → Tully
days.summary: Cross McGee Pass into the western basin.
directions: Return to the McGee Pass trail and assess the pass before committing.
Cross only with acceptable current snow, wind and footing; retain time to retreat.
Continue down the western side and take the mapped Tully Lake branch to a legal site.
days.warning: Snow and ice can make an established trail impassable. This is a planning itinerary, not current field clearance. McGee Pass is roughly 11,900 feet; the return also requires crossing it.

days.title: Tully ↔ Virginia → Big McGee
days.summary: Optional JMT lake visit, then return over the pass.
directions: Retrace the Tully branch to McGee Pass trail, follow it toward the JMT/PCT, then take the northbound JMT/PCT to Lake Virginia.
Return on the same trails to Tully; skip this optional excursion if conditions or daylight reduce your margin.
Return east over McGee Pass to Big McGee Lake and a legal site.
days.warning: Snow and ice can make an established trail impassable. This is a planning itinerary, not current field clearance. This is the longest day at about 15 mapped miles, before camps and shore detours.

days.title: Big McGee → trailhead
days.summary: Descend the same canyon.
directions: Retrace the Big McGee branch and descend McGee Pass trail to the trailhead.
Finish at the authorized McGee Creek parking spot.
days.warning: Snow and ice can make an established trail impassable. This is a planning itinerary, not current field clearance.

checks.title: Confirm McGee Creek Road and overnight parking
checks.body: Ask about the final road condition, overnight spaces and any early snow closure.

checks.title: Reserve JM05 for Oct 13, one person
checks.body: Book the matching entry, exit Oct 16 and one continuous trip. Browser quota snapshot is not a reservation.

checks.title: Get a fresh snow, ice and water report
checks.body: McGee Pass is crossed twice; obtain a current report. Cut the optional Virginia outing if daylight or weather reduces the return margin.

sabrina.label: Sabrina Basin
sabrina.intro: Hungry Packer base with the Midnight Lake trail outing. Baboon cairn-marked path is omitted under your Class 2 constraint.
sabrina.recommendation: Best of these three for avoiding a major crest-pass crossing, subject to actual snow and icy trail conditions. It still reaches an exposed alpine basin. The Baboon branch includes a cairn-marked path and deserves extra route-finding care.

days.title: Sabrina → Hungry Packer
days.summary: Blue Lake, Dingleberry country and the crest basin.
directions: Park in the signed overnight turnout near the North Lake turnoff, as described by the Forest Service; the lake-end lot is day use. Confirm current signs and Hwy 168 access.
Walk to the Sabrina trailhead; that road approach is extra to the mapped mileage.
Follow Sabrina Basin trail past Blue Lake; take the right fork toward Dingleberry and the Hungry Packer branch.
Choose a legal durable site at least 100 feet from water and trail.
days.warning: Snow and ice can make an established trail impassable. This is a planning itinerary, not current field clearance. Road walking from overnight parking is not included in the 26.5-mile total.

days.title: Hungry Packer ↔ Midnight
days.summary: A short mapped lake outing.
directions: Return to the Sabrina Basin junction and take the Midnight Lake branch.
Retrace to the same legal Hungry Packer camp.
Keep optional lake-edge exploration reversible and away from steep icy terrain.
days.warning: Snow and ice can make an established trail impassable. This is a planning itinerary, not current field clearance.

days.title: Hungry Packer · flexible day
days.summary: Rest, established trail viewpoints, or an earlier exit.
directions: Remain on established trails and accessible trail-side viewpoints near Hungry Packer.
The cairn-marked Baboon branch is excluded because its Class 2 ceiling is not verified.
Exit early if snow, ice or current conditions exceed your limit.
days.warning: No additional walking distance is counted for a flexible day. Your campsite and road approach add mileage.

days.title: Hungry Packer → Sabrina
days.summary: Reverse the basin trail and return to overnight parking.
directions: Retrace the Hungry Packer and Sabrina Basin trails to the trailhead.
Continue on the road to the signed overnight parking area.
days.warning: Snow and ice can make an established trail impassable. This is a planning itinerary, not current field clearance. Road walk adds distance on the exit as well.

checks.title: Use Sabrina’s signed overnight turnout
checks.body: USDA identifies the turnout near the North Lake turnoff; the lake-end lot is day use. Confirm current signs and Hwy 168 access. Road walking adds distance both ways.

checks.title: Reserve JM17 for Oct 13, one person
checks.body: Book the matching entry, exit Oct 16 and one continuous trip. Browser quota snapshot is not a reservation.

checks.title: Get a fresh snow, ice and water report
checks.body: Hungry Packer basin and the cairn-marked Baboon branch need fresh footing/navigation reports. Keep the lake outings optional.

checks.title: Confirm the exact overnight parking spot
checks.body: Ask whether you may leave the car October 13–16 at Horseshoe Lake, and whether Lake Mary Road will remain accessible. The published “day use” description establishes facilities, not overnight permission.

checks.title: Confirm the legal construction bypass
checks.body: Current order 05-04-52-26-19 closes Reds Meadow Road plus 200 feet on either side on weekdays. Comparing our mapped approach with USFS road geometry gives a minimum separation of about 342 metres, outside that corridor. This is map evidence, not current field clearance; confirm the exact trail connection with a ranger.

checks.title: Get a fresh trail snow / ice report
checks.body: Ask about Minaret, JMT passes, Ediza and the Cecile–Iceberg corridor. The forecast and historic photographs are not current field observations.
